Azelis (+8.2% organic in Q3) and IMCD (+14% organic EBITA) both printed after the three bearish previews the market is holding, and the guide arithmetic (H1 769m plus ~380m leaves only ~250m for Q4 against Q4 2025's 268m) points to an upper-half narrowing -- but at $16m a day with sixteen-plus analysts these peer prints are read by everyone, so the sizes are modest, and the free-cash-flow line, which Azelis and BASF both flag and no visible note addresses, is the offsetting negative on a name whose investment case rests on FCF.

The buyback finding is the one thing in this pack that nobody aggregates: the share count has been frozen at 155,754,560 since 25 June, the weekly TIOS RNS stopped, and the ~$45.6m left on the $50m programme is only visible by subtracting across three separate announcements -- the same hurricane-season pause this issuer lifted in its Q3 2025 update (+2.91%), worth about 5% of market cap on a stock at 0.78x June TNAV with the register covering; against it the Middle East political-violence reserve is a live, unquantified downside that Arch has already booked and Conduit's own CEO sized at ~$4bn industry-wide.

Brent from ~$71 to ~$100 across Q3 against the company's own statement that oil volatility 'increased the lag impact in the freight pass-through model' is a real but unquantified macro-to-company transmission, and the Q3 volumes are fully pre-released in three monthly releases so they are worth almost nothing; the absence of any nedjustering six weeks after quarter end bounds the downside, Tallink held EBITDA flat through the same fuel environment, and the strategy-review signals are genuinely two-sided, so p_up only leans.

Near-zero: twelve analysts model the monthly portability data the hunt rests on, the Telefonica wholesale read is a Q2 data point already inside Digi's reported H1 margin and reiterated guide, and the guidance arithmetic (H1 515m against 1,040-1,085m) says reiteration, which the European base prices at about 2.3%; the auditor change is immaterial to an unaudited quarter, and with no readable CNMV register this name has no positioning anchor at all, so nothing here can beat the run-up control.

The company's own numbers put the 'rund EUR 1.2bn' guide under strain -- H1 636.2m at +0.9% needs H2 of about 563.8m against 527.5m, roughly +6.9% -- while the only visible consensus (three analysts) still sits at 1.2bn and the 9M release is the scheduled moment this issuer narrowed last year; Bunnings telling the Wesfarmers AGM on 29 Oct that FY27 year-to-date growth 'has moderated' is a dated counterparty statement on the exact market Einhell's H1 flagged declining, and no German preview mentions it, and this name has fallen on its last three confirmations, while +6.35% in five sessions on thin volume is not what a priced-in trim looks like; Hornbach's +7.3% quarter is the honest offset on the 61% that is Western Europe.

This is the setup the stage exists for: Volvo CE's Q3 North America deliveries +41% (1,911 vs 1,352) and order intake +80% were published on 23 Oct, a week AFTER the only sourceable bar -- a single commissioned ABG estimate assuming +11% group sales -- and that estimate has not been revised, on a name with $122k/day of turnover, no non-commissioned coverage and a reaction distribution that has paid +23.2%, +13.6% and +23.8% for exactly this kind of beat; abs_move is sized on that distribution and not on the 5.43% cadence median, p_up stops at 67 because dealer deliveries are a proxy for Rudd's retail sales, part reverses 2025 destocking and management pre-tempered Q3 as a quarter that 'will vary'.

The run-rate case is real -- quarterly adj. EBITDA deltas of -4.6m and -10.7m with about 28m of the ~50m MNO hit left for H2 carry FY to roughly 490-500 against a company-compiled consensus of 509, whose implied Q4 of ~136m is 16m above Q4 2025 -- but it is arithmetic the nine contributing analysts can do from the same file, which caps it well below the 9% guidance-change base; the EUR 75m buyback and the waipu.tv buyout are public and the stock is +4.8% in five sessions, so the capital-return leg offsets part of it, and the Telefonica renegotiation is a low-probability right tail.

First report since the 20.04% LEG stake, and whether GCP books pro-rata LEG FFO into its own FFO I -- which would carry FY to about 190-195m against a 175-185m guide -- has not been stated by anyone, so a guidance raise is a live and unpriced accounting question; what holds the size down is that the stock is already +20.4% over 20 days and +11.9% over five, the parent has publicly put the accretion at ~15%, the one-off is explicitly non-cash on a stock at 30% of NTA, and Berenberg's refinancing question is the real negative on the half of EUR 1.4bn of liquidity now spent.

Everything found is priced by construction: the Europe IX final close was public on 9 September and the company itself published the Visible Alpha consensus on 27 October, so the analysts sat above the Q1-plus-Europe-IX sum of about $5.23bn knowingly, the one-third-of-prior-year interim dividend is mechanical, and a fundraising-target reset belongs at full-year results; at $22.9m a day with a sourced company-compiled bar there is no coverage gap to exploit, and the only residual is the ~$0.7bn of unannounced Q2 flows.

Offsetting and close to nothing: the EUR 29-30m licensing one-off that flattered last year's Q1 was disclosed a year ago and restated in the FY release, so analysts model it out and only the 07:00 wire headline on a $0.7m/day SDAX name is left, and the rapeseed-area item is market commentary (EU -2%, France -10-15%) against an issuer that calls rapeseed its strongest crop; on the other side the de-rating is done -- the guide was reset below consensus on 23 September for -9.0% -- so a plain confirmation lands on a reset bar, and the net is a non-result.

The working-capital line is the one the measured European lesson says to look at before signing the name, and it is where this stock has sold off twice (-7.63% on Q3 2025 and -6.63% on Q3 2024 with NFP in the release): Kepler nearly doubled its FY net-debt estimate to 50m on an inventory build, and the 30 September NFP is undisclosed; with the sell-side sitting at the top of a range that implies H2 EBITDA of only 45-50m against 44.6m, a plain reiteration reads as a mild disappointment, and Ingram Micro's +7.3% EMEA quarter is the honest counter the market pointedly did not extrapolate. Session read is amc with timestamps, so the findings sit in the 11-12 Nov window.

Genuinely offsetting on a name where both sides are public: the EUR 3.4bn guide against a company-compiled consensus implying about 3.37bn is a mild beat lean that sixteen-plus analysts and a $62.9m/day tape have already read, and the last print that beat and confirmed was sold 3.65%, with the stock now up 5.45% in five sessions into this one; the ANIA series mixes channels and points both ways, and the TIM step-acquisition remeasurement adds size to the move without giving it a sign.

Olvi's Q3 Finland volume -4.4% and its 13 October tulosvaroitus on freight and packaging cost are a dated counterparty read on one of Royal Unibrew's two largest markets against a Q3 2025 comp the company itself called a strong Finnish quarter, and the stock has instead tracked sector beta (+13% against Carlsberg +17% and Heineken +19%) rather than marking Finland down; the reiterated guide needs H2 EBITDA of 1,299-1,399m against 1,243m after a 4.4% Q2 miss, so a low-or-middle narrowing is likelier than a move up -- trimmed because the Danish register is already building, no nedjustering has been filed, and Carlsberg's solid Nordic volumes plus a dry, sunny Danish summer cut the other way on the largest market.

The FOI indexation of the 2027 RAI contract at 5.2-5.3% against estimates built on ~1% is a real unpriced item -- the company consensus was compiled on 30 October, before the 2 November note, and the stock has not moved since -- but it is one broker's reading of a contract formula, it lands in 2027 revenue, and the issuer releases in session around 15:30-16:30 CET with the call at 18:00, so this window holds only an hour or so of reaction and the indexation question is most likely answered after it; abs_move is cut for that, which is why the number is small rather than the finding being weak.

Revenue and the raised guide were pre-released by ad-hoc on 7 October, so the quarter's headline lines are worth 0 and the release turns on order intake and backlog -- the line that carried +9.9% on the last full report, for which no consensus is sourceable; the company publicises large monthly intake (it announced June's >EUR 100m) and has announced nothing since, so a step down from Q1's 149.4m and Q2's 180.8m and a book-to-bill near 1 is the likely print, with Rheinmetall's Arminius slip adding to the 2027 phasing question. It is an inference from absence on a lumpy defence order book, which is why p_up stays within 10 of 50 while abs_move is sized on a 47%-vol name whose only observed print day moved 9.9%.

A large move with no defensible sign: the order shortfall is pre-released and consensus already cut to 3,388 MW with only Citi's 0.7-0.8 GW unannounced residual left, Nordex's 12.7% Q3 margin and FY raise are public and were traded on 16 October, and on the other side the company-compiled bar of 8.4% against a 7-9% guide requires a Q4 margin of about 10.5% after a 9M of 7.5%, above Q2's 9.4% peak -- so where management centres the narrowed range decides everything and nothing in the evidence says which way; abs_move is held high because guide changes have moved this name +19.7%, +14.8% and -8.7%, and all of the uncertainty goes into p_up at 50.
